LESSON: FICTION AND NON - FICTION 7.3.1 FICTION: ANTHOLOGY OF SHORT STORIES FROM KENYA

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: LITERATURE IN ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.3: Fiction and Non - Fiction 7.3.1 Fiction: Anthology of Short Stories from Kenya
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Fiction and Non - Fiction 7.3.1 Fiction: Anthology of Short Stories from Kenya, part of Strand 7 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 LITERATURE IN ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How do characters in short stories reflect our society? 2. Why should we pick moral lessons from short stories?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify the setting and plot of the short story for literary appreciation,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Fiction and Non - Fiction 7.3.1 Fiction: Anthology of Short Stories from Kenya in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. analyse the characters and their traits for literary analysis,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Fiction and Non - Fiction 7.3.1 Fiction: Anthology of Short Stories from Kenya in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate the value of the short story for life- long learning.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Fiction and Non - Fiction 7.3.1 Fiction: Anthology of Short Stories from Kenya in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify the setting and plot of the short story for literary appreciation,

   Fiction and Non - Fiction 7.3.1 Fiction: Anthology of Short Stories from Kenya helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. analyse the characters and their traits for literary analysis,

   Fiction and Non - Fiction 7.3.1 Fiction: Anthology of Short Stories from Kenya helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate the value of the short story for life- long learning.

   Fiction and Non - Fiction 7.3.1 Fiction: Anthology of Short Stories from Kenya helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read the short story and discuss the setting. Learners with speech difficulties could be given more considerable time.

2. team up to write down the sequence of events. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted writing tools and materials.

3. present the sequence of events in the short story on a flow chart in class,

4. identify the characters in the short story and their traits,

5. practise hot seating for various characters,

6. link the characters to real life and draw lessons,

7. collaborate to present a summary of the characters and their relationship with others in a graphic organiser and display it in the classroom, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read the short story and discuss the setting. Learners with speech difficulties could be given more considerable time.
2. team up to write down the sequence of events. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted writing tools and materials.
3. present the sequence of events in the short story on a flow chart in class,
4. identify the characters in the short story and their traits,
5. practise hot seating for various characters,
6. link the characters to real life and draw lessons,
7. collaborate to present a summary of the characters and their relationship with others in a graphic organiser and display it in the classroom, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Fiction and Non - Fiction 7.3.1 Fiction: Anthology of Short Stories from Kenya together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and problem solving: This is enhanced as the learner uses logical thinking to present the sequence of events

in the short story on a flow chart in class.

● Creativity and imagination: This is nurtured as the learner embraces creative ideas when practising hot seating for various

characters.

Values:
● Social justice: This is enhanced as the learner accords equal opportunities to peers when collaborating to present a summary

of the characters and their relationship with others in a graphic organiser and displays it in the classroom.

● Respect: This is nurtured as the learner appreciates peer’s contributions when picking out the moral lessons from the short

story.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social awareness skills: This is enhanced as the learner collaborates with peers to accomplish group tasks.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. identify the setting and plot of the short story for literary appreciation,
2. analyse the characters and their traits for literary analysis,
3. appreciate the value of the short story for life- long learning.

Remember the key question: How do characters in short stories reflect our society? 2. Why should we pick moral lessons from short stories?
